title: Fifty Days Out. India Is About to Host the Biggest Badminton Tournament on Earth.
excerpt: The BWF World Championships return to New Delhi after 17 years with Sindhu, Lakshya Sen, Satwik-Chirag, and a resurgent Srikanth all playing on home soil — and tickets start at just ₹499.
body:
The countdown clock started ticking on Sunday. Exactly 49 days from now, the world's best shuttlers will walk onto the courts at the Indira Gandhi Arena in New Delhi for the 30th edition of the BWF World Championships — and for the first time in 17 years, India will be the host.

It is the biggest event in badminton outside the Olympics, and India has never had a stronger squad to showcase on home turf.

## A Homecoming Worth Planning For

The last time India hosted the World Championships was 2009 in Hyderabad, when a teenaged PV Sindhu sat in the stands as a spectator. This time, Sindhu — a five-time World Championship medallist including the 2019 gold, and India's most decorated badminton player — will walk out as the host nation's wildcard entrant. It is widely expected to be one of her final appearances on the biggest stage.

Lakshya Sen, currently ranked 11th in the world and India's highest-ranked men's singles player, qualified in the host nation's top spot. At 24, he enters the tournament as a genuine medal contender — a bronze medallist in 2021, a Commonwealth Games gold medallist, and one of the most consistent performers on the BWF World Tour this year.

Then there are Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, the men's doubles pair who made history as the first Indians to medal in the discipline at a World Championship (bronze, 2022). They will compete at a BWF Worlds on home soil for the first time.

And Kidambi Srikanth, who reached the US Open final in Fullerton, California just this past weekend — saving three match points in the semifinal before falling to Su Li Yang in the final — has shown he is far from done. The 2021 World Championship silver medallist's form heading into the home event is the best it has been in two years.

Rounding out India's emerging depth is 22-year-old Ayush Shetty, who has climbed to 18th in the world qualification rankings and earned a second singles spot for India — a sign of how far the country's badminton pipeline has come.

## The Global Field

The qualification list, finalised based on the April 28 World Ranking, confirms that all five defending champions will be in New Delhi. China's Shi Yu Qi leads the men's singles draw as the top-ranked qualifier, while defending women's champion Akane Yamaguchi of Japan enters at third. South Korean pair Kim Won Ho and Seo Seung Jae return to defend their men's doubles title, and Liu Sheng Shu and Tan Ning of China will defend the women's doubles crown.

Emerging powerhouse France has three qualifiers in men's singles — the same number as China, Japan, and Denmark. The traditional South-East Asian powers — Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand — are all strongly represented across every category.

In all, 64 qualifiers each in men's and women's singles and 48 pairs in each of the three doubles events will compete across seven days from August 17 to 23.

## Tickets Are Live — and Surprisingly Affordable

The Badminton Association of India announced BookMyShow as the official ticketing partner on June 22, with over 6,000 seats available to the general public across six seating categories. Early Bird tickets start at just ₹499 — roughly $6 — with premium matchday seating at ₹5,500. A 15 per cent Early Bird discount is available across the upper five categories for a limited time.

"Our ambition is not just to host a world-class tournament, but to deliver a fan experience that matches the occasion," said BAI General Secretary Sanjay Mishra.

## Why NRIs Should Pay Attention

For Indian diaspora fans in the US, UK, and Canada, this is a rare convergence: a world championship-level event in India, in August when summer schedules are flexible, with affordable tickets and a home squad stacked with medal contenders. The last time India hosted an event of this calibre in badminton, the country had zero World Championship gold medals. Now Sindhu alone has five medals, and the depth runs four or five players deep.

Srikanth's US Open run in California last week gave American-based fans a live preview of the kind of atmosphere a world-class Indian shuttler can generate. New Delhi will be that, amplified.

Ticket sales are being released in phases on BookMyShow, beginning with the opening four days of competition. Category pricing remains consistent through to the finals.

The venue — the Indira Gandhi Arena, the same facility that hosted the 2010 Commonwealth Games badminton events — was also the site of the India Open 2026 Super 750 in January, which served as a dress rehearsal for the World Championships.

India's record at the BWF World Championships now spans 15 podium finishes since 1983. If form, home crowd, and timing mean anything, that number is about to grow.
